rows.note: This is the all-purpose Cantonese noun for an intentionally false statement.

example.jyutping: nei5 m4 hou2 zoi3 gong2 daai6 waa6 laa3

rows.note: Use 講大話 as the all-purpose colloquial choice when someone intentionally gives false information.

example.english: Those people lie all the time, so don't trust them.
example.traditional: 嗰班人成日講大話，唔好信佢哋。
example.jyutping: go2 baan1 jan4 seng4 jat6 gong2 daai6 waa6 m4 hou2 seon3 keoi5 dei6

rows.note: Use 瞓 for a person lying down or resting horizontally, usually with a place complement.

example.english: I'm so tired I need to lie on the sofa.
example.jyutping: ngo5 gui6 dou3 jiu3 fan3 so1 faa3

rows.note: Use 喺 when saying where a place or object is situated.

example.english: The book can lie on the table.
example.jyutping: bun2 syu1 ho2 ji5 hai2 zoeng1 toi2 soeng6 min6

rows.note: Use 留喺 when emphasizing that something remains in a particular condition or state.

example.english: That shirt can lie on the chair for now.
example.jyutping: gin6 saam1 zaam6 si4 lau4 hai2 zoeng1 dang3 dou6
